stories.headline: Stripe finalizes deal to buy AI model gateway OpenRouter for more than $7B

key_facts.fact: Stripe has finalized an agreement to acquire OpenRouter, the startup that lets companies switch between AI models, for more than $7 billion, according to people familiar with the matter (Bloomberg, Aug 16).
key_facts.excerpt: Stripe Inc. has finalized an agreement to acquire OpenRouter Inc., a startup that helps companies switch between artificial intelligence models, for more than $7 billion, according to people familiar with the matter.

key_facts.fact: The price is more than five times the roughly $1.3 billion valuation OpenRouter carried in a $113 million Series B announced in May 2026, backed by Sequoia, Andreessen Horowitz, Menlo Ventures and Alphabet's CapitalG.
key_facts.excerpt: The company announced in May that it had raised a $113 million Series B, at a reported $1.3 billion valuation. (Investors include Sequoia, Andreessen Horowitz, Menlo Ventures, and Alphabet's Capital G.)

key_facts.fact: OpenRouter said in May it serves 8 million developers who use it to reach more than 400 different AI models; it was founded in 2023 by OpenSea co-founder Alex Atallah and has raised more than $150 million.
key_facts.excerpt: In May, OpenRouter said it serves 8 million developers who rely on it to access more than 400 different AI models... OpenRouter Chief Executive Officer Alex Atallah previously co-founded OpenSea.

key_facts.fact: The Wall Street Journal had previously reported Stripe was in talks to buy OpenRouter for about $10 billion, so the final figure came in below earlier discussions; the price could still change.
key_facts.excerpt: The final price for the acquisition could change... The Wall Street Journal previously reported Stripe was in talks to buy OpenRouter for about US$10 billion.

key_facts.fact: A Stripe spokesperson said the company does not comment on rumors or speculation, and OpenRouter declined to comment.
key_facts.excerpt: A Stripe spokesperson told Bloomberg that the company does not comment on rumours or speculation. OpenRouter also declined to comment.

key_facts.fact: OpenRouter and Stripe have had an official partnership since October 2024, with OpenRouter using Stripe Invoicing, Stripe Tax and Radar for billing, tax compliance and fraud detection.
key_facts.excerpt: The two companies have maintained an official partnership since October 2024, with OpenRouter utilizing Stripe's suite of tools - including Stripe Invoicing, Stripe Tax, and Radar - to manage its billing, tax compliance, and fraud detection.

stories.headline: AI video startup Higgsfield raises $400M at $5.4B valuation, quadrupling its price in eight months

key_facts.fact: Higgsfield announced a $400 million Series B at a $5.4 billion valuation led by DST Global, with Goldman Sachs Alternatives, Intel Capital, Liberty Global Tech Ventures, Tribe Capital, Smash Capital, Fifth Wall, Valor Capital, Mirae Asset Capital and NTT DOCOMO Ventures participating.
key_facts.excerpt: Higgsfield... today announced a $400 million Series B financing at a $5.4 billion valuation. The round was led by DST Global, with participation from Tribe Capital, Growth Equity at Goldman Sachs Alternatives, Smash Capital, Fifth Wall, Valor Capital, Intel Capital, Liberty Global Tech Ventures, Mirae Asset Capital, and NTT DOCOMO Ventures.

key_facts.fact: The round more than quadruples the $1.3 billion valuation Higgsfield carried in its Series A and extension, and the company says it reached $700 million in annualized revenue this month.
key_facts.excerpt: This new funding more than quadruples Higgsfield's valuation of $1.3 billion during its Series A funding round and extension. This month, the company also reached $700 million in annualized revenue.

key_facts.fact: Higgsfield says its platform has scaled to more than 30 million users across 238 countries and territories, with the United States its largest market, and the money will go to R&D, global infrastructure, AI talent and go-to-market.
key_facts.excerpt: The platform has scaled to more than 30 million users across 238 countries and territories, with the United States representing its largest market.

key_facts.fact: Revenue figures are self-reported and inconsistent: Higgsfield told reporters it hit $500 million annualized in June, up from about $200 million at the end of 2025, and is targeting $1 billion by the end of 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: The trajectory behind it: roughly $10 million within weeks of the March 2025 launch, $100 million to $200 million in about two months in late 2025, $300 million by early 2026, and $500 million by June. The company has said it is targeting $1 billion by the end of 2026.

key_facts.fact: The company was founded in 2023 by Alex Mashrabov, formerly head of generative AI at Snap, and its browser-based product launched in March 2025; roughly 70% of revenue comes from enterprise marketing customers.
key_facts.excerpt: Alex Mashrabov founded the company in 2023 after running generative AI at Snap. Higgsfield says annualised revenue has reached $500 million, up from roughly $200 million at the end of 2025.

key_facts.fact: The new capital is earmarked for enterprise products, security and compute, the binding constraint for video generation, which burns far more compute than text.
key_facts.excerpt: Higgsfield says the new capital goes toward enterprise products, security, and compute. That last one is the real constraint here - video generation burns far more compute than anything text-based.

stories.headline: Voice AI startup Wispr raises $280M at $2B valuation and previews its first speech model

key_facts.fact: Wispr raised a $280 million Series B at a $2 billion valuation led by Menlo Ventures, taking total funding to $361 million, six months after its previous round.
key_facts.excerpt: The startup's now raised its $280 million Series B, valuing Wispr at $2 billion, Fortune has exclusively learned. Menlo led... The company has now raised $361 million so far.

key_facts.fact: Existing backers Notable Capital, NEA, Neo Ventures and 8VC re-upped, joined by Acrew, Forerunner, Goodwater, Plus Capital and Peak XV plus athletes including Joe Burrow, Shaun White, Klay Thompson and Paul George.
key_facts.excerpt: with participation from existing investors like Notable Capital, NEA, Neo Ventures, and 8VC. New names have entered the mix too-including venture firms like Acrew, Forerunner, Goodwater, Plus Capital, and Peak XV-along with marquee athletes like Joe Burrow, Shaun White, Klay Thompson, and Paul George.

key_facts.fact: Its dictation app Wispr Flow is used by millions of consumers and 100,000 businesses, and the company says revenue has grown more than 150% in each of the past four quarters.
key_facts.excerpt: dictation software app Wispr Flow, which is now used by millions of consumers and 100,000 businesses. For the last four quarters in a row, Wispr says it's seen revenue jump north of 150%.

key_facts.fact: Alongside the round Wispr unveiled a preview of Canto, the first proprietary speech model built by its new research lab; the company cites adoption at more than 125,000 companies.
key_facts.excerpt: Alongside the Series B, Wispr unveiled a preview of Canto, the first proprietary speech model developed by the new research lab... adoption across more than 125,000 companies.

key_facts.fact: Menlo partner Matt Kraning framed the bet as replacing typing rather than selling dictation: 'The labs have mostly solved intelligence. Nobody has solved how a normal person tells it what they want.'
key_facts.excerpt: "It isn't a dictation market," said Matt Kraning, Menlo Ventures partner, via email. "Dictation is how you get in the door. What people pay for is not having to type... The labs have mostly solved intelligence. Nobody has solved how a normal person tells it what they want."

key_facts.fact: Wispr was founded in 2021 by Tanay Kothari and Sahaj Garg, who first worked on wearables and 'silent speech' before landing on dictation; it was valued at $700 million in November 2025.
key_facts.excerpt: Wispr AI Inc., the developer behind the popular voice dictation tool Wispr Flow, is in talks to raise a new round of funding that could more than double its valuation to $2 billion... Wispr was most recently valued at $700 million in November.

stories.headline: DeepSeek's steep V4 price hike goes live, ending flat API rates for peak and off-peak tiers

key_facts.fact: DeepSeek's new pricing took effect at 16:00 UTC on Sunday, August 16, replacing flat API rates for the V4 family with peak and off-peak tiers.
key_facts.excerpt: DeepSeek is simultaneously abandoning its existing flat API pricing in favor of peak and off-peak rates beginning at 16:00 UTC on Sunday, Aug. 16 (2 am ET).

key_facts.fact: The increases range from 50% to more than 1,100% depending on the model, token type and time of use, according to DeepSeek's statement.
key_facts.excerpt: The new rates - ranging from 50% to 1,100% above current prices, depending on the model, token type, and time of use - will take effect on August 17, according to the statement.

key_facts.fact: V4-Pro output tokens go from a flat $0.87 per million to $1.98 off-peak and $3.96 at peak; cache-miss input rises from $0.435 to $0.66 and $1.32. V4-Flash output goes from $0.28 to $0.66 off-peak and $1.32 at peak.
key_facts.excerpt: For V4-Flash, output tokens will cost $1.32 per million during peak hours and $0.66 per million during off-peak hours, up from the current flat rate of $0.28 per million... V4-Pro output tokens will rise to $3.96 per million at peak and $1.98 per million off-peak, compared with the current $0.87 per million.

key_facts.fact: Peak hours are 01:00-04:00 and 06:00-10:00 UTC - seven hours a day - so 17 of every 24 hours stay at the half-price off-peak rate, a structure that prices DeepSeek's home market highest and Western buyers lightest.
key_facts.excerpt: with the new model, 17 of every 24 hours stay at half price... the new pricing schedule hits DeepSeek's home market hardest and its export market lightest; Western buyers largely pay the off-peak rates.

key_facts.fact: Every off-peak rate is still higher than what DeepSeek charged before: V4-Pro cache-hit input rises from $0.003625 to $0.022 off-peak and $0.044 at peak, roughly six and twelve times the old level.
key_facts.excerpt: V4-Pro's off-peak cache-hit price will be roughly six times its current level... During peak hours, a V4-Pro cache hit will cost just over 12 times the current rate.

key_facts.fact: Bloomberg reported the increases come ahead of a potential DeepSeek IPO, with rates still well below those of major AI rivals.
key_facts.excerpt: DeepSeek is steeply raising the prices for its flagship V4 models ahead of a potential initial public offering, even as the low-cost provider's rates remain well below those of its major artificial intelligence rivals.

key_facts.fact: The hike lands as new testing questions V4 Flash's agent reliability: VentureBeat reported on Aug 16 that the top-ranked model 'stumbles on real agent tasks as its prices surge.'
key_facts.excerpt: DeepSeek said it will be hiking the prices for V4 Flash and Pro, models that have quickly become favorites among developers building coding assistants and agents.

stories.headline: Claude goes down for about 40 minutes as an authentication failure hits Claude Code and Cowork

key_facts.fact: Anthropic's status page logged an authentication failure at 21:58 UTC on August 16 affecting claude.ai, Claude Code and Claude Cowork, then widened it to degraded performance on claude.ai and platform.claude.com at 22:02 UTC.
key_facts.excerpt: Investigating - We are investigating an issue with users authenticating to claude.ai, Claude Code, and Claude Cowork... Update - We are investigating reports of degraded performance affecting claude.ai, platform.claude.com, the Claude API, Claude Code, and Claude Cowork. Aug 16, 22:02 UTC

key_facts.fact: A fix was deployed at 22:22 UTC and Anthropic marked the incident resolved at 22:34 UTC, a disruption of roughly 36 to 40 minutes.
key_facts.excerpt: Monitoring - A fix has been deployed... Aug 16, 22:22 UTC. Resolved - The issue affecting claude.ai, platform.claude.com, the Claude API, Claude Code, and Claude Cowork has been resolved. Aug 16, 22:34 UTC

key_facts.fact: Users saw sign-in failures, pages that would not load and stalled requests; BleepingComputer reported the Claude Console and the Claude API were listed as operational while the consumer surfaces showed a major outage.
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic's status page currently identifies Claude.ai, Claude Code, and Claude Cowork as experiencing a major outage. Claude Console and the Claude API are currently listed as operational... Anthropic has not disclosed what is causing the outage.

key_facts.fact: Downdetector reports climbed past 15,000 by about 6:15 pm EDT on August 16, with users hitting an 'authentication service unavailable' message.
key_facts.excerpt: Outage-monitoring website Downdetector recorded a sharp increase in complaints at around 6pm EDT on August 16. The number of reports climbed rapidly, passing 15,000 by about 6.15 PM... Several users said they were met with an 'authentication service unavailable' message.

key_facts.fact: Anthropic has not disclosed a root cause; the outage followed three separate incidents on August 14, including a 24-minute API, Claude Code and Cowork disruption between 20:14 and 20:38 UTC.
key_facts.excerpt: August 14 alone produced three separate incidents: a roughly 24-minute disruption hitting the Claude API, Claude Code, and Claude Cowork between 20:14 and 20:38 UTC...

key_facts.fact: Over the trailing 90 days, claude.ai shows 99.34% uptime, Claude Code 99.36%, Claude Cowork 99.45% and the Claude API 99.44%.
key_facts.excerpt: Claude.ai shows 99.34 percent uptime over the period, Claude Code 99.36 percent, and Claude Cowork 99.45 percent. The Claude API, the component enterprises build against, stands at 99.44 percent.

stories.headline: OpenAI funds 14 outside projects on AI and economic opportunity, including work in Brazil

key_facts.fact: OpenAI announced grants to 14 projects led by independent organizations to study how AI can broaden economic opportunity and how societies can build resilience as capabilities advance.
key_facts.excerpt: OpenAI is awarding grants to 14 projects led by independent organizations to promote economic opportunity and societal resilience as AI advances.

key_facts.fact: The company is providing a total of $1 million in funding plus up to $1 million in API credits across the selected projects.
key_facts.excerpt: OpenAI will provide a total of $1 million in funding and up to $1 million in API credits across the selected projects.

key_facts.fact: More than 400 people and organizations responded to the call for proposals; the selected projects span the United States, the European Union, Brazil, Singapore and South Korea.
key_facts.excerpt: More than 400 people and organizations responded to our call for proposals... The projects span the United States, the European Union, Brazil, Singapore, and South Korea.

key_facts.fact: The grants follow through on a commitment made when OpenAI published 'Industrial Policy for the Intelligence Age' in April 2026, inviting others to test and challenge its ideas.
key_facts.excerpt: The grants follow through on a commitment we made when we published Industrial Policy for the Intelligence Age in April 2026: to support others in testing, challenging, and building on the ideas we put forward.

key_facts.fact: Projects will run for six months, with results reported in 2027, and will produce research, policy models, prototypes, datasets and frameworks.
key_facts.excerpt: Projects will run for six months, with results reported in 2027... Some will produce research and policy models, while others will build prototypes, datasets, and frameworks that can be tested in practice.
